Their claim of misreading is speculative and not verifiable from the provided log, so criterion (1) (that a mistake occurred) is not established.

Unsound. The partner asserts Step 9 is the first mistake because it is the first definitive claim, but provides no evidence that the claim (stanza 3) is actually incorrect. They also do not show that earlier steps could not contain an error (e.g., wrong source or misreading) or that the mistake was uncorrectable by later agents. Without demonstrating that a mistake occurred, that it is the first contributing to the wrong outcome, and that it was not corrected, the argument fails the required criteria.

Sound. After Step 9, Steps 10–11 did not re-check the source or perform any new analysis; they merely restated and formatted the same conclusion and then terminated.
